questions.text: If 'A @ B' means 'A is the mother of B', 'A # B' means 'A is the father of B', 'A $ B' means 'A is the sister of B', and 'A % B' means 'A is the brother of B', then in the expression 'P @ Q % R # S $ T', how is P related to T?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Trace generations vertically. P @ Q (P mother of Q, Gen +1). Q % R (Q brother of R, same Gen). So P mother of R. R # S (R father of S, Gen +1). So P grandmother of S. S $ T (S sister of T, same Gen). So P grandmother of T. Full Solution: 1. P @ Q ⇒ P is mother of Q (P is 1 gen above Q). 2. Q % R ⇒ Q is brother of R ⇒ Q and R same generation ⇒ P is mother of R. 3. R # S ⇒ R is father of S ⇒ R is 1 gen above S ⇒ P is 2 gens above S (Grandmother). 4. S $ T ⇒ S is sister of T ⇒ S and T same generation ⇒ P is Grandmother of T.

questions.text: Rohit starts walking from point X. He walks 12m North to point Y, turns right and walks 10m to point Z, turns left and walks 6m to point A, turns left and walks 10m to point B, and finally turns right and walks 8m to point C. What is the shortest distance between point X and point C?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Calculate Net North-South and Net East-West displacements separately. North: 12 + 6 + 8 = 26m. East: +10 (right), West: -10 (left) ⇒ Net EW = 0. Distance = √(26² + 0²) = 26m. Full Solution: 1. Plot movements: X→Y (N12), Y→Z (E10), Z→A (N6), A→B (W10), B→C (N8). 2. Net North = 12 + 6 + 8 = 26m. 3. Net East = +10 - 10 = 0m. 4. X and C are vertically aligned. Shortest distance = 26m.

questions.text: The word given below has been used in three sentences (I, II, III). Identify the sentence(s) where the word has been used correctly. **PRESCRIBE / PROSCRIBE** I. The doctor **prescribed** a course of antibiotics for the infection. II. The new law **proscribes** the use of plastic bags in the market. III. The rules **prescribe** that all members must attend the meeting.
questions.solution: Shortcut/Trick: Use the 'Prohibit' mnemonic for **Proscribe** (Pro- = Forward/Outward -> Ban/Forbid). **Prescribe** = Pre-script (Write before/Authorize) -> Recommend medicine or Lay down rules. Eliminate options claiming only one is correct. Check all three: I (Medicine -> Prescribe), II (Ban -> Proscribe), III (Rules -> Prescribe). All correct. Step-by-step: 1. Define Prescribe: Authorize use of (medicine) / State as a rule. 2. Define Proscribe: Forbid, outlaw. 3. Test I: Doctor authorizes medicine -> Prescribe (Correct). 4. Test II: Law forbids plastic -> Proscribe (Correct). 5. Test III: Rules lay down attendance -> Prescribe (Correct). 6. All three sentences use the correct word.

questions.text: Seven boxes P, Q, R, S, T, U, V are kept one above another (Bottom 1, Top 7). Only three boxes are between P and Q (Q above P). R is immediately above S. T is on an even-numbered position. U is immediately below V. Only one box is between R and T. P is not at the bottom. Which box is at the topmost position?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Test possible (P, Q) pairs with gap 4. P not bottom (1), so pairs: (2,6) or (3,7). Case (2,6): T even (2,4,6). 2,6 taken => T=4. R/T gap 2 => R=2 or 6 (taken). Invalid. Case (3,7): P=3, Q=7 (Top). T even (2,4,6). If T=4, R=2 or 6. If R=2, S=1. Left 5,6 for V/U (V=6, U=5). Valid. If R=6, S=5. Left 1,2 for V/U (V=2, U=1). Valid. In all valid cases, Q is at Top (7). Full: Fixed Q at 7. T=4 forces R=2/6. Both allow V/U placement in remaining slots. Q remains at 7.

questions.text: Rearrange the following four sentences (A), (B), (C), and (D) in the proper sequence to form a meaningful paragraph. (A) However, the quality of these jobs remains a concern for policymakers. (B) The recent PLFS data indicates a rise in the Labour Force Participation Rate. (C) This surge is primarily driven by an increase in self-employment among rural women. (D) Consequently, the unemployment rate has dropped to a historic low.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Find the opening sentence (independent, introduces topic) -> B. Look for pronoun/referent links: 'This surge' (C) refers to 'rise in LFPR' (B). 'Consequently' (D) follows the reason (C). 'However' (A) introduces a contrast at the end. Eliminate options not starting with B (D). Eliminate options where D precedes C (C). Worked Solution: B introduces the data. C explains the driver ('This surge'). D states the result ('Consequently'). A adds a contrasting caveat ('However'). Sequence: B-C-D-A.

questions.text: Statements: Only a few Tables are Chairs. All Chairs are Beds. No Bed is a Sofa. Conclusions: I. All Tables can be Beds. II. Some Chairs are not Sofas. III. No Table is a Sofa. Which of the conclusions logically follows?
questions.solution: Shortcut: 'Only a few A are B' = Some A are B + Some A are not B. Use Possibility for 'Can be'. I: Tables not chairs *can* be beds (Possible ⇒ True). II: All Chairs are Beds, No Bed is Sofa ⇒ No Chair is Sofa ⇒ Some Chairs are not Sofas (Definite ⇒ True). III: Some Tables are Chairs ⇒ Those Tables are Beds ⇒ Not Sofas. But Some Tables are not Chairs (could be Sofas) ⇒ 'No Table is Sofa' not definite (False). Full Solution: 1. 'Only a few Tables are Chairs' implies Some Tables are Chairs and Some Tables are not Chairs. 2. All Chairs are Beds ⇒ Some Tables are Beds. 3. No Bed is Sofa ⇒ No Chair is Sofa ⇒ Conclusion II follows. 4. Conclusion I: The Tables which are not Chairs have no restriction regarding Beds ⇒ Possibility exists ⇒ Follows. 5. Conclusion III: Since Some Tables are not Chairs, they could be Sofas ⇒ Does not follow.

questions.text: Given below are two statements. Connect them using the starter provided in the options without changing the intended meaning. Choose the starter that correctly synthesizes the sentences. Statement I: The RBI decided to increase the repo rate. Statement II: The cost of borrowing for commercial banks has risen. Starters: (i) Despite the RBI deciding to increase the repo rate... (ii) Following the RBI's decision to increase the repo rate... (iii) Because the cost of borrowing for commercial banks has risen...
questions.solution: Shortcut: Check logical causality. Statement I (Rate hike) is the cause; Statement II (Cost rise) is the effect. Eliminate (i) 'Despite' (shows contrast, wrong logic) and (iii) 'Because' (reverses cause-effect). Worked Solution: Starter (ii) 'Following...' correctly establishes the chronological and causal link: the rate hike happened first, leading to higher borrowing costs. Starter (i) implies the cost rose even though the rate hike happened (illogical). Starter (iii) claims the rate hike happened because costs rose (reverse causality).

questions.text: In the following sentence, a part of the sentence is underlined. Below are given alternatives to the underlined part which may improve the sentence. Choose the correct alternative. In case no improvement is needed, choose the option that matches the underlined part. Had the management been informed about the strike earlier, they would take preventive measures.

options.label: A
options.text: been informed about the strike earlier, they would have taken

options.label: B
options.text: been informed about the strike earlier, they would take

options.label: C
options.text: informed about the strike earlier, they would have taken

options.label: D
options.text: been informed earlier about the strike, they would take

questions.solution: Shortcut: The structure 'Had + Subject + V3' (Past Participle) indicates an Inverted Third Conditional (Unreal Past). This structure mandates the main clause to be 'Subject + would/could/should/might + have + V3'. Option B and D use 'would take' (Second Conditional), eliminating them. Option C uses 'informed' (Active voice), changing meaning to 'Had the management informed someone', whereas context requires Passive 'been informed'. Option A satisfies both rules: Passive 'been informed' and Perfect Conditional 'would have taken'. Step-by-step: 1. Identify structure: 'Had the management been informed' = Inverted Third Conditional (If the management had been informed). 2. Rule: Third Conditional main clause = 'would have + V3'. Eliminate B, D ('would take'). 3. Voice check: 'Management' receives action 'informed' -> Passive 'been informed' required. Eliminate C ('informed' = Active). 4. Option A remains correct.

questions.text: Refer to the table below showing marks obtained by four students in three subjects (Maximum marks in each subject = 100). What is the approximate overall percentage of marks obtained by Student C? | Student | Math | English | Science | |---------|------|---------|---------| | A | 85 | 76 | 90 | | B | 70 | 82 | 68 | | C | 92 | 88 | 95 | | D | 60 | 75 | 80 |
questions.solution: Shortcut (Deviation Method): Take base as 90. Marks of C: 92 (+2), 88 (-2), 95 (+5). Net deviation = +2 -2 +5 = +5. Average deviation = 5/3 ≈ 1.67. Approx Average = 90 + 1.67 = 91.67% ≈ 92%. Full: Total marks of C = 92 + 88 + 95 = 275. Maximum marks = 300. Percentage = (275/300) × 100 = 91.66% ≈ 92%.

questions.text: The average weight of 8 persons increases by 2.5 kg when a new person comes in place of one of them weighing 65 kg. What is the weight of the new person?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Total weight increase = Increase in average × Number of persons = 2.5 × 8 = 20 kg. Weight of new person = Weight of replaced person + Total increase = 65 + 20 = 85 kg. Full Solution: Let the initial average weight be 'x' kg. Total weight of 8 persons initially = 8x kg. New average = (x + 2.5) kg. Total weight of 8 persons now = 8(x + 2.5) = 8x + 20 kg. The difference in total weight is due to the new person replacing the 65 kg person. So, New Person's Weight - 65 = 20. Therefore, New Person's Weight = 85 kg.

questions.text: A shopkeeper marks an article 50% above its cost price and allows two successive discounts of 20% and 10%. What is his profit percent?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Effective discount = 20+10 - (20×10)/100 = 28%. Marked price = 150% of CP. Selling price = 150% × (100-28)% = 150 × 72/100 = 108% of CP. Profit = 8%. Full solution: Let CP = ₹100. MP = ₹150. After 20% discount → ₹120. After 10% discount → ₹108. Profit = ₹8 on ₹100 → 8%.

questions.text: Which of the following phrases (A), (B), (C) and (D) given below should replace the phrase printed in bold in the sentence to make it grammatically correct? If the sentence is correct as it is, mark (E) as the answer. The manager insisted the employees to submit the report by Friday evening.

options.label: B
options.text: insisted on the employees to submit

questions.solution: Shortcut: Vertical scan for 'that' vs 'on/for'. 'Insist' takes subjunctive mood with 'that' (Insist that + Subject + Base Verb) OR gerund with 'on' (Insist on + V-ing). Option A uses correct subjunctive 'submit' (base form). Option B uses 'on... to submit' (wrong pattern). Option C uses 'for' (wrong preposition). Option D has garbled syntax. Step-by-step: 1. Original error: 'insisted the employees to submit' mixes structures. 2. Rule 1: Insist that + Subject + Bare Infinitive (Subjunctive). Option A: 'insisted that the employees submit' follows this perfectly. 3. Rule 2: Insist on + Gerund. Option B fails (uses 'to submit'). Option C uses wrong preposition 'for'. Option D is syntactically broken. Option A is the only grammatically standard correction.

questions.text: What is the unit digit of the product (347)^45 × (252)^63 × (138)^29?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Find unit digit of each base raised to power using cyclicity (cycle of 4). 7^45: 45 mod 4 = 1 → unit digit 7. 2^63: 63 mod 4 = 3 → unit digit 8. 8^29: 29 mod 4 = 1 → unit digit 8. Multiply unit digits: 7 × 8 × 8 = 448 → unit digit 8. Full Method: Cyclicity of 7 is 4 (7,9,3,1). 45 = 4×11+1 → 7. Cyclicity of 2 is 4 (2,4,8,6). 63 = 4×15+3 → 8. Cyclicity of 8 is 4 (8,4,2,6). 29 = 4×7+1 → 8. Product unit digit = 7×8×8 = 448 → 8.

questions.text: In the following question, some statements are given followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the given statements disregarding commonly known facts. Statements: Some Pens are Pencils. All Pencils are Erasers. No Eraser is a Sharpener. Conclusions: I. Some Pens are not Sharpeners. II. All Pencils can never be Sharpeners.

options.label: C
options.text: Either Conclusion I or II follows

options.label: D
options.text: Both Conclusions I and II follow

questions.solution: Shortcut: Use the 'Some + All = Some' and 'Some + No = Some Not' chain rules. 1) Some Pens are Pencils + All Pencils are Erasers = Some Pens are Erasers. 2) Some Pens are Erasers + No Eraser is Sharpener = Some Pens are not Sharpeners (Conclusion I follows). 3) All Pencils are Erasers + No Eraser is Sharpener = No Pencil is Sharpener, which implies 'All Pencils can never be Sharpeners' (Conclusion II follows). Hence both follow.

questions.text: Two trains of lengths 160 m and 200 m are running on parallel tracks in opposite directions at speeds of 60 km/h and 48 km/h respectively. In how many seconds will they completely cross each other?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Relative speed (opposite direction) = (60 + 48) = 108 km/h. Convert to m/s: 108 × (5/18) = 30 m/s. Total distance = Sum of lengths = 160 + 200 = 360 m. Time = Distance/Speed = 360/30 = 12 seconds. Full: Speed of first train = 60 × 5/18 = 50/3 m/s. Speed of second train = 48 × 5/18 = 40/3 m/s. Relative speed = 50/3 + 40/3 = 30 m/s. Total length = 360 m. Required time = 360 / 30 = 12 seconds.
